LESSON: SINGING GAMES- AFRICAN STYLE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.1: Singing Games- African Style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Singing Games- African Style, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are singing games performed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify singing games in African style,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Singing Games- African Style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Singing Games- African Style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: as the learner confidently makes a variety of body movements which are appropriate while performing the

African singing games.

● Learning to learn: as the learner performs African singing games while making different pattern formations learnt in

earlier grades,

● Citizenship: as the learner takes pride in performing African singing games from diverse Kenyan communities.

Values:
● Responsibility is promoted as the learner takes different roles while performing an African style singing game.

● Unity is promoted as the learner works with others as they perform African style singing games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Personal hygiene is enhanced as the learner collects locally available materials for making simple paper costumes.

● Self-awareness and self-esteem is promoted as the learner makes a variety of movements which are appropriate while

performing the singing game in African style.

Link to other learning areas:

Indigenous Language Activities as the learners sing varied indigenous songs in the African singing games.

Suggested learning resources:

Audio or visual recordings of African style singing games, props, papers, pair of scissors, adhesives, adapted tools and

materials such as looped scissors, scissors with grip, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces,

adapted digital devices, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page- turners, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand,

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist,

Physiotherapist.
